stem: Which of the following is true of paediatric airway foreign bodies?

options.text: The diagnostic triad of cough, wheeze and unilaterally diminished breath sounds is present in the majority of cases
The most sensitive diagnostic factor for airway foreign body is a history of witnessed choking/coughing/gagging episode
A young child presenting with recurrent pneumonia should raise the suspicion of airway foreign body
Foreign bodies are more likely to lodge in the left main bronchus
A reasonable suspicion mandates exploratory/diagnostic bronchoscopy

explanation: Paediatric airway foreign body aspiration can present subtly, and recurrent or non-resolving pneumonia in a young child should prompt suspicion. The other statements are incorrect or overstated: the classic triad is not present in most cases, a witnessed choking episode is helpful but not the single most sensitive factor, foreign bodies more commonly lodge in the right main bronchus, and bronchoscopy is indicated when suspicion is significant but not simply mandated by every low-level concern.
rationale: This is the only option that is clearly true as written and preserves the original clinical concept without needing rewrite.

optionExplanations.A: The classic triad is not present in the majority of cases.
optionExplanations.B: A witnessed choking episode is important, but this is not the best-described most sensitive factor.
optionExplanations.C: Correct — recurrent pneumonia in a young child should raise suspicion of an airway foreign body.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect — foreign bodies more commonly lodge in the right main bronchus.
optionExplanations.E: Suspicion may warrant bronchoscopy, but the wording is too absolute as a universal rule.
